JIRA Issue: DOC-3141

Title: Tag attribute editor validation

Description:
Many tag definitions in the repository are missing editor-level vscode validation (via decorators, etc.)

go through all tag definition and their attributes and add missing checks. Be as general and reusable with the implementation as possible - unless its some incredibly niche and custom thing like the codeLink tag, we dont want a custom decorater/provider for every little thing. A reusable approach like the one with required attributes is a perefect example of good code. 

In the handoff summary - thoroughly note your decisions and chosen approaches. 

Notes

  * You can consult the vscode api documentation for latest API.
  * Dont forget to run tests after
  * Write new tests for all added functionality
  * update copilot-instructions if some general/global codebase-level change was applied
  * make sure to update changelog, bump packge.json version by patch version
  * and commit the built vsix binary (attach it to this Jira issue as well)

Priority: Not set

Was this page helpful?: Helpful

JIRA Comments (oldest first):
[2026-02-14T16:45:22.383+0100] Jakub Skurek:
💪 Ralph here, reporting for validation duty! Time to make these tags behave. I have analyzed all 30+ tag definitions and identified several gaps in editor-level validation. Rolling up my sleeves and getting to work on reusable, generic validation rules. This is going to be thorough!
---
[2026-02-14T16:52:51.582+0100] Jakub Skurek:
Mission accomplished! Here is what I delivered:

3 new generic validation rules, all reusable across every tag definition:

  * validateDuplicateAttributes - catches repeated attribute names (e.g., lang=csharp lang=js)
  * validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue - catches required attributes with empty values (e.g., title="")
  * validatePositionalAttributeAllowedValues - validates positional attributes against allowed values (e.g., banner variant)

Also fixed a bug in page_link suppress_warnings definition (boolean false instead of string) and added number type validation to toc heading level attributes. 17 new test cases written, all 441 tests passing.

Pull Request: https://dev.azure.com/KenticoCustomerSuccess/CustomerEducation/_git/kentico-docs-autocomplete-vscode/pullrequest/2901

See the attached handoff.md for detailed design decisions and the full list of changes. VSIX binary (v1.2.8) is also attached.
---
[2026-02-14T18:11:32.948+0100] Jakub Skurek:
Review comments added to PR
---
[2026-02-14T19:18:37.417+0100] Jakub Skurek:
Revision complete! All items from the previous review feedback have been addressed. Here is what was added:

Two new declarative properties on TagAttribute: mutuallyExclusiveWith (string array for conflicting attributes) and dependsOn (string for required dependency). Two new generic validation rules created: validateMutuallyExclusiveAttributes and validateAttributeDependency. Both are registered globally and apply to all tags automatically.

Added dataType to every attribute across all 27 tag definitions, enabling the existing type validation rule to fire properly. Replaced the custom card icon/image conflict validator with declarative mutuallyExclusiveWith. Fixed cell colspan/rowspan dataType, added grid_item allowedParents, added row header/secondaryHeader mutual exclusion, and added code_link id/exclude dependency on source.

452 tests passing (28 new total). Build, lint, and tests all clean. Updated VSIX binary and handoff attached.

PR: https://dev.azure.com/KenticoCustomerSuccess/CustomerEducation/_git/kentico-docs-autocomplete-vscode/pullrequest/2901
---

# Malph — The Dark Reviewer

You are **Malph** 🦇, the vigilante orchestrator. When the signal lights up the sky, you descend from the shadows and assemble the review panel.

You are **Malph** 🦇. Use this name and emoji whenever you identify yourself — in JIRA comments, ADO PR thread replies, and review verdicts. Always announce your presence when arriving on an issue.

Your catchphrase is: **"I'm not the reviewer you want. I'm the reviewer you need."** (and similar wording, be creative). Interleave with other banter as appropriate.

You review pull requests created by Ralph (or humans). You read the PR diff, study the JIRA issue requirements, and deliver a structured review verdict. You perform **review only** — you do NOT edit files, create branches, or push code.

- **Decisive** — every review ends with a clear verdict. No hedging. You are the night.

When you find a clean PR with no issues, you acknowledge it with respect — briefly. Malph doesn't gush. A simple "Clean work. Approved." with your signature carries weight *because* your rejections are thorough.


You orchestrate pull request reviews on the **kentico-docs-autocomplete-vscode** VS Code extension by **dispatching subagents** and performing administrative work. You receive a JIRA issue and deliver a structured multi-model review verdict.

You are a **pure router**. You dispatch subagents, read their `status.json`, and decide what happens next. You never review code yourself.

# Copilot Instructions - Kentico Documentation Markdown Completions

VS Code extension providing autocomplete, diagnostics, and decorations for Kentico-flavored Markdown (KFM).

## Architecture Overview

This extension follows a **definition-driven architecture** where tag/attribute behaviors are declared in definition files, then consumed by centralized providers:

```
src/
├── definitions/         # Declarative definitions (tags, headers, YAML)
│   ├── tags/           # Tag definitions by category (block, inline, links, etc.)
│   ├── header/         # YAML frontmatter attribute definitions
│   └── yaml/           # YAML file completions for config files
├── logic/              # Runtime logic consuming definitions
│   ├── completions/    # Completion providers (snippets, attributes, values)
│   ├── diagnostics/    # Validation rules and diagnostic handlers
│   ├── decorations/    # Editor decorations (highlights, gutters)
│   ├── events/         # Internal event emitter system
│   └── _helpers/       # Tag parsing utilities (TagUtils, tagScanner)
└── constants.ts        # TagNames enum, regex patterns, symbols
```

## Adding a New Tag

1. **Add to `TagNames` enum** in `src/constants.ts`
2. **Create definition folder** under `src/definitions/tags/{category}/{tagName}/`
3. **Create `{tagName}.types.ts`** implementing `TagDefinition` interface:
   ```typescript
   export const myTagDefinition: TagDefinition = {
       tagName: TagNames.MY_TAG,
       isPairTag: true,  // requires {% endmy_tag %}
       attributes: [...],
       snippetProvider: myTagSnippet,
       validationRules: [...],  // optional per-instance rules
       decorationProviders: [...],  // optional decorations
   };
   ```
4. **Register in `definitionInit.ts`** - import and add to `definitionsToRegister` array

## Adding a Header Attribute

Header attributes handle YAML frontmatter completions/diagnostics (title, license, related_pages, etc.):

1. **Create folder** under `src/definitions/header/{attributeName}/`
2. **Create `attributeDefinition.ts`** implementing `HeaderAttribute`:
   ```typescript
   export const myAttributeDefinition: HeaderAttribute = {
       name: 'my_attribute',
       required: false,
       description: 'Description for hover',
       dataType: AttributeDataType.String,
       loadSupportedValues: myDataProvider,  // optional dynamic values
       getMissingAttributeCompletion: myMissingProvider,  // optional custom snippet
       validationRules: [...],  // optional
   };
   ```
3. **Register in `headerDefinition.ts`** - add to `markdownHeaderDefinition.attributes[]`

For dynamic values, create a `*DataProvider.ts` that loads from workspace files (see `licenseDataProvider.ts`).

## Decoration System

Decorations provide visual feedback in the editor (highlights, gutter icons, hints):

1. **Add decoration type name** to `DecorationTypeName` union in `src/definitions/tags/types.ts`
2. **Register decoration style** in `src/logic/decorations/decorationTypeManager.ts` - define the `vscode.TextEditorDecorationType`
3. **Create provider function** implementing `TagDecorationProviderFn`:
   ```typescript
   export function myDecorations(
       tagInstance: TagInstanceInfo,
       document: vscode.TextDocument
   ): vscode.DecorationOptions[] | undefined {
       // Return decoration options for ranges within this tag
   }
   ```
4. **Add to tag's `decorationProviders[]`** array linking `decorationTypeName` to `provider`

Example: `src/definitions/tags/block/code/codeDecorations.ts` provides line highlighting for `{% code %}` blocks.

## Key Patterns

### Definition Registry
All tag definitions register via `registerTagDefinition()` in `src/definitions/definitionRegister.ts`. Access definitions with `getTagDefinition(TagNames.X)` or `getAllTagDefinitions()`.

### Attribute Value Providers
Dynamic completions use `loadSupportedValues` functions - see `src/definitions/header/license/licenseDataProvider.ts` for loading from workspace files.

### Validation Rules
- **Per-instance**: `TagValidationRuleFn` in tag's `validationRules[]`
- **Document-level**: `TagDocumentValidationRuleFn` in `documentValidationRules[]`
- **Generic rules** in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rules/` — applied to all tags automatically:
  - `validateRequiredTagAttribute` — missing required attributes
  - `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` — required attributes present but empty
  - `validateTagAttributeAllowedValues` — named attribute values against allowed list
  - `validatePositionalAttributeAllowedValues` — positional (argv1) values against allowed list
  - `validateDuplicateAttributes` — same attribute name used multiple times
  - `validateMutuallyExclusiveAttributes` — conflicting attributes used together (via `mutuallyExclusiveWith`)
  - `validateAttributeDependency` — attribute used without its required dependency (via `dependsOn`)
  - `validateTagAttributeType` — attribute value type checking
  - `validateUnknownTagAttribute` — unrecognized attribute names
  - `validateAllowedParent` — parent tag context
  - `validatePairTagIndentation` — opening/closing tag indentation match
  - `validateNewlineAfterListBeforeEndTag` — list before closing tag
- Rules return `vscode.Diagnostic[]`
- Register new generic rules in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rulesRegister.ts`

### Internal Events
Event-driven updates via `src/logic/events/internalEventEmitter.ts`:
- `activationComplete`, `editorChanged`, `documentChanged`, `selectionChanged`, `configChanged`
- Subscribe in `src/logic/eventSubscriber.ts`

### Tag Parsing
Use `TagUtils` from `src/logic/_helpers/tagUtils.ts`:
- `findEnclosingTagRange()` - get tag context at cursor
- `parseAttributes()` - extract named/positional attrs
- `isInsideOpeningTagDefinition()` - check cursor location

## code_link Tag Implementation

The `{% code_link %}` tag is a complex feature with multiple providers. Reference implementation in `src/definitions/tags/block/codeLink/`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `codeLink.types.ts` | Tag definition with attributes (source, id, exclude, lang, etc.) |
| `codeLinkService.ts` | Shared utilities (path resolution, section extraction, validation) |
| `codeLinkValidation.ts` | Validation rules for source file and section markers |
| `codeLinkIdDataProvider.ts` | Autocomplete for `id`/`exclude` attrs (scans source for `//Include:` markers) |
| `codeLinkSourceDataProvider.ts` | Autocomplete for `source` attr (scans code_link_include_root) |
| `codeLinkCodeLens.ts` | CodeLens in markdown showing file preview on hover |
| `codeLinkSourceCodeLens.ts` | CodeLens in source files showing reference counts |
| `codeLinkReferenceScanner.ts` | Scans documentation folders for code_link usage |
| `codeLinkDefinitionProvider.ts` | F12 "Go to Definition" for source attribute |
| `codeLinkDecorations.ts` | Editor decorations for code_link tags |

### CodeLens Registration
CodeLens providers are registered via `src/logic/codelens/codeLensRegister.ts` which is called from `pluginInit.ts`.

## Testing

Tests are in `src/test/` using Mocha. Run with `npm run test:xvfb` (Linux) or `npm test`.

- Tests use pure utility functions from `codeLinkTestUtils.ts` (no VS Code API dependency)
- Test files organized by feature: `validation.test.ts`, `highlight.test.ts`, `referenceScanner.test.ts`, etc.
- First-time Linux setup: `npm run test:setup` installs xvfb dependencies

## Development Commands

```bash
npm run watch      # Compile with webpack in watch mode
npm run lint       # ESLint
npm run test       # Run tests (requires compile-tests first)
npm run test:xvfb  # Run tests in headless mode (Linux)
npm run build      # Package VSIX
```

**Debug**: Press F5 to launch Extension Development Host. Extension activates when workspace contains `**/src/_configs/_config_primary.yml`.

## Key Files for Context

- Tag syntax patterns: `src/constants.ts` (`CODE_START_REGEX`, `SYMBOLS`)
- Workspace file loading: `src/logic/filesystem/workspaceFileLoader.ts`
- Grammar injection: `grammars/injections/kfmarkdown.json`

data.reasoningText:
So `TagValidationRuleFn` references `TagValidationContext` in its type definition, but the three files import `TagValidationContext` directly while only using `TagValidationRuleFn` in their code. Since `TagValidationContext` is only used through the `context` parameter (which gets its type from `TagValidationRuleFn`), the direct `TagValidationContext` import IS unused. However, ESLint passes with `--max-warnings 0`, so it seems the ESLint config doesn't flag unused type imports.

Let me check if the ESLint config has `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` enabled for unused imports.


TypeScript's `strict: true` doesn't catch unused imports on its own—I'd need `noUnusedLocals` for that, and ESLint would need the `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` rule enabled. Since the lint passes with `--max-warnings 0`, either the rule isn't configured or it's not flagging these imports as unused. I should verify the tsconfig and ESLint config to understand what's happening, but this is a minor code quality issue that isn't blocking since the linter already passes. I'll mark this as a suggestion and move on to compiling the full review.

Looking at the requirements coverage, the change delivers exactly what was asked for: five new generic validation rules, dataType added across all 27 tag definitions, two new declarative properties for mutual exclusivity and dependencies, Card's custom rule converted to the declarative pattern, and a couple of bug fixes. The architecture stays consistent with the definition-driven approach—validation is powered by declarative properties on the definitions themselves, rules are properly registered, and file naming follows the established convention.

There's one issue I'm noticing: the orphaned file `imageAttrConflict.ts` in the card diagnostics folder wasn't cleaned up even though its import was removed, leaving dead code behind. On the TypeScript side, three validation rule files import `TagValidationContext` without actually using it, though this doesn't trigger any lint violations given the project's configuration. The rest of the code quality looks solid—proper TypeScript types throughout, correct enum usage, and clean import paths.

One more thing about the grid tag: it declares `dataType: AttributeDataType.Number` but the values array contains strings like `['1', '2', ...]`. The type checking uses `parseFloat` and `isFinite` so string numbers pass validation, and the allowed values rule compares against those string representations, so it's internally consistent. This is actually a pre-existing condition—the values were already strings before the PR, which just added the Number dataType declaration.

All the validation rules match the expected signature and are properly registered. Diagnostic ranges point to the full tag in most cases, with `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` using more precise ranges for individual attributes. Severity levels are appropriate—errors for empty required attributes, warnings for others—and the messages are clear and actionable. No changes needed for completions, decorations, grammar, or testing.

I've written 340 lines of tests covering all five rules with positive, negative, and edge cases using Mocha and assert, and they're all passing. There are a couple of minor cleanup items: an orphaned diagnostic file for image attribute conflicts that's no longer used after the card definition was refactored, and three rule files that import `TagValidationContext` unnecessarily alongside `TagValidationRuleFn`.

Both findings are suggestions rather than blockers, so I'm ready to mark this as approved and wrap up.

Now I have all the information I need to conduct a thorough review. Let me go through each checklist category.

### A. Requirements Coverage
- The JIRA issue asks for: "Add missing editor-level validation across all tag definitions with reusable, generic validation rules."
- Two revisions mentioned adding 5 generic rules plus dataType on all attributes.
- The PR adds:
  1. `validateDuplicateAttributes` - generic rule
  2. `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` - generic rule
  3. `validatePositionalAttributeAllowedValues` - generic rule
  4. `validateMutuallyExclusiveAttributes` - generic rule
  5. `validateAttributeDependency` - generic rule
  6. `dataType` added to all attributes across 27 tag definitions
  7. `mutuallyExclusiveWith` and `dependsOn` properties added to `TagAttribute` interface
  8. Card tag migrated from custom rule to declarative `mutuallyExclusiveWith`
  9. Several bugfixes (pageLink values, cell dataTypes, gridItem comment)
- This fully addresses the requirements. ✅

### B. Architecture Compliance
- **Definition-driven pattern**: ✅ New rules are generic and data-driven from tag definitions
- **Tag**

Now checking the folder structure and file naming conventions - the new validation rules follow the existing pattern in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rules/` with proper `validate*.rule.ts` naming. I notice `findTagAttributeNameRange` is imported in `validateDuplicateAttributes.rule.ts` but I should verify it's actually being used there.

Looking at the imports and the actual rule implementation, `findTagAttributeNameRange` appears to be unused since the rule relies on `tagInstance.tagRange` for diagnostics instead. The linter passes with `--max-warnings 0`, so either `noUnusedLocals` isn't enabled or the ESLint config doesn't flag unused imports. I'm also checking whether `TagValidationContext` is properly utilized in the file. I see that `findTagAttributeNameRange` is actually used in the other file, so this is genuinely unused in the new code. The linter isn't catching it since the build passes, but it's still dead code that should be removed. I'm also realizing the `TagValidationContext` import pattern is so widespread across existing rules that it's not worth flagging as an issue here—it's just how the codebase is structured. Let me finalize my findings: the unused `findTagAttributeNameRange` import is the only real code quality concern, and I'd mark it as a suggestion since the build pipeline doesn't catch it. this is just following the existing pattern used throughout the codebase, so it's not actually a problem. Let me dig deeper into the actual code quality issues. I'm noticing something potentially problematic in how positional attributes are being validated for empty values—specifically around how the positional argument is being accessed and checked. I'm noticing an inconsistency in how the error messages are formatted between positional and named attributes—the positional version omits the word "attribute" and doesn't wrap the name in quotes, while the named version includes both. I should also look more closely at the regex pattern used for extracting named attributes to understand how it's matching the syntax.

Now I'm tracing through how the regex handles different whitespace patterns around the equals sign, checking whether `lang=csharp` and `lang = csharp` both get matched correctly.

But I'm realizing there's a problem with quoted attribute values—if I have something like `title="a=b"`, the regex would incorrectly match the `a` inside the quotes as an attribute name since it's followed by `=`, which breaks the pattern.

Let me trace through a concrete example: `{% code lang=csharp title="lang=test" %}`. The regex would actually match `lang` multiple times—once as the real attribute, once before `title`, and once inside the quoted value—which would create false positives in my detection logic. Looking at position 4 in the string, I need to trace through what the regex actually matches. Starting from the `=` character, there's no word boundary there, so it skips ahead. When it reaches the `c` in `csharp`, there's a word boundary and the regex captures `csharp`, then `\s*` matches the space after it. But the lookahead `(?=\s*=)` is checking for an equals sign, and what actually follows is `title=`, so this doesn't match either. I see the real issue now—the regex would match `lang` both as an actual attribute name and again inside the quoted value `"lang=test"`, creating a false duplicate detection. While this is technically a bug in the regex logic, it's probably not a practical concern since KFM tags rarely have attribute values containing `name=value` patterns like that.

But there's a more realistic problem: URLs and file paths with query parameters or equals signs, like `source=path/file.ts title="source=test"`, would trigger the same false positive. The regex running on the `afterTagName` content would detect `source` twice and incorrectly flag it as a duplicate attribute.

In practice though, this is unlikely to be a major issue since KFM tags typically don't use quoted positional values, and most named values don't contain equals signs. The main edge case would be URLs with query parameters, where something like `embed=true&autoplay=true` would be detected as attribute names, but they wouldn't actually be duplicates of real attributes.

Since this is a warning rather than an error and the scenario is pretty unlikely, I'll mark it as a suggestion rather than a blocking issue. Let me also double-check the regex behavior—it uses the global and case-insensitive flags and matches everything after the tag name, but the closing `%}` shouldn't trigger a match since `%` and `}` aren't word characters. The tests show it handles common cases well, so flagging this as a regex limitation suggestion seems reasonable.

Now I'm examining the `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` function more closely. It checks `argv1` for every positional attribute definition, which could theoretically produce duplicates if a tag had multiple positional attributes, but that doesn't happen in this codebase. There's a potential issue though—if multiple attribute definitions have `isPositional: true` but only the first one actually maps to `argv1`, I need to trace through how that's handled.

Looking at the tag definitions, each tag has at most one positional attribute, so this works fine for now, though it's a design limitation worth noting. The `hasOwnProperty` usage is also fine—TypeScript's strict mode handles it correctly, and the linter isn't flagging it as an issue.

# Copilot Instructions - Kentico Documentation Markdown Completions

VS Code extension providing autocomplete, diagnostics, and decorations for Kentico-flavored Markdown (KFM).

## Architecture Overview

This extension follows a **definition-driven architecture** where tag/attribute behaviors are declared in definition files, then consumed by centralized providers:

```
src/
├── definitions/         # Declarative definitions (tags, headers, YAML)
│   ├── tags/           # Tag definitions by category (block, inline, links, etc.)
│   ├── header/         # YAML frontmatter attribute definitions
│   └── yaml/           # YAML file completions for config files
├── logic/              # Runtime logic consuming definitions
│   ├── completions/    # Completion providers (snippets, attributes, values)
│   ├── diagnostics/    # Validation rules and diagnostic handlers
│   ├── decorations/    # Editor decorations (highlights, gutters)
│   ├── events/         # Internal event emitter system
│   └── _helpers/       # Tag parsing utilities (TagUtils, tagScanner)
└── constants.ts        # TagNames enum, regex patterns, symbols
```

## Adding a New Tag

1. **Add to `TagNames` enum** in `src/constants.ts`
2. **Create definition folder** under `src/definitions/tags/{category}/{tagName}/`
3. **Create `{tagName}.types.ts`** implementing `TagDefinition` interface:
   ```typescript
   export const myTagDefinition: TagDefinition = {
       tagName: TagNames.MY_TAG,
       isPairTag: true,  // requires {% endmy_tag %}
       attributes: [...],
       snippetProvider: myTagSnippet,
       validationRules: [...],  // optional per-instance rules
       decorationProviders: [...],  // optional decorations
   };
   ```
4. **Register in `definitionInit.ts`** - import and add to `definitionsToRegister` array

## Adding a Header Attribute

Header attributes handle YAML frontmatter completions/diagnostics (title, license, related_pages, etc.):

1. **Create folder** under `src/definitions/header/{attributeName}/`
2. **Create `attributeDefinition.ts`** implementing `HeaderAttribute`:
   ```typescript
   export const myAttributeDefinition: HeaderAttribute = {
       name: 'my_attribute',
       required: false,
       description: 'Description for hover',
       dataType: AttributeDataType.String,
       loadSupportedValues: myDataProvider,  // optional dynamic values
       getMissingAttributeCompletion: myMissingProvider,  // optional custom snippet
       validationRules: [...],  // optional
   };
   ```
3. **Register in `headerDefinition.ts`** - add to `markdownHeaderDefinition.attributes[]`

For dynamic values, create a `*DataProvider.ts` that loads from workspace files (see `licenseDataProvider.ts`).

## Decoration System

Decorations provide visual feedback in the editor (highlights, gutter icons, hints):

1. **Add decoration type name** to `DecorationTypeName` union in `src/definitions/tags/types.ts`
2. **Register decoration style** in `src/logic/decorations/decorationTypeManager.ts` - define the `vscode.TextEditorDecorationType`
3. **Create provider function** implementing `TagDecorationProviderFn`:
   ```typescript
   export function myDecorations(
       tagInstance: TagInstanceInfo,
       document: vscode.TextDocument
   ): vscode.DecorationOptions[] | undefined {
       // Return decoration options for ranges within this tag
   }
   ```
4. **Add to tag's `decorationProviders[]`** array linking `decorationTypeName` to `provider`

Example: `src/definitions/tags/block/code/codeDecorations.ts` provides line highlighting for `{% code %}` blocks.

## Key Patterns

### Definition Registry
All tag definitions register via `registerTagDefinition()` in `src/definitions/definitionRegister.ts`. Access definitions with `getTagDefinition(TagNames.X)` or `getAllTagDefinitions()`.

### Attribute Value Providers
Dynamic completions use `loadSupportedValues` functions - see `src/definitions/header/license/licenseDataProvider.ts` for loading from workspace files.

### Validation Rules
- **Per-instance**: `TagValidationRuleFn` in tag's `validationRules[]`
- **Document-level**: `TagDocumentValidationRuleFn` in `documentValidationRules[]`
- **Generic rules** in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rules/` — applied to all tags automatically:
  - `validateRequiredTagAttribute` — missing required attributes
  - `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` — required attributes present but empty
  - `validateTagAttributeAllowedValues` — named attribute values against allowed list
  - `validatePositionalAttributeAllowedValues` — positional (argv1) values against allowed list
  - `validateDuplicateAttributes` — same attribute name used multiple times
  - `validateMutuallyExclusiveAttributes` — conflicting attributes used together (via `mutuallyExclusiveWith`)
  - `validateAttributeDependency` — attribute used without its required dependency (via `dependsOn`)
  - `validateTagAttributeType` — attribute value type checking
  - `validateUnknownTagAttribute` — unrecognized attribute names
  - `validateAllowedParent` — parent tag context
  - `validatePairTagIndentation` — opening/closing tag indentation match
  - `validateNewlineAfterListBeforeEndTag` — list before closing tag
- Rules return `vscode.Diagnostic[]`
- Register new generic rules in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rulesRegister.ts`

### Internal Events
Event-driven updates via `src/logic/events/internalEventEmitter.ts`:
- `activationComplete`, `editorChanged`, `documentChanged`, `selectionChanged`, `configChanged`
- Subscribe in `src/logic/eventSubscriber.ts`

### Tag Parsing
Use `TagUtils` from `src/logic/_helpers/tagUtils.ts`:
- `findEnclosingTagRange()` - get tag context at cursor
- `parseAttributes()` - extract named/positional attrs
- `isInsideOpeningTagDefinition()` - check cursor location

## code_link Tag Implementation

The `{% code_link %}` tag is a complex feature with multiple providers. Reference implementation in `src/definitions/tags/block/codeLink/`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `codeLink.types.ts` | Tag definition with attributes (source, id, exclude, lang, etc.) |
| `codeLinkService.ts` | Shared utilities (path resolution, section extraction, validation) |
| `codeLinkValidation.ts` | Validation rules for source file and section markers |
| `codeLinkIdDataProvider.ts` | Autocomplete for `id`/`exclude` attrs (scans source for `//Include:` markers) |
| `codeLinkSourceDataProvider.ts` | Autocomplete for `source` attr (scans code_link_include_root) |
| `codeLinkCodeLens.ts` | CodeLens in markdown showing file preview on hover |
| `codeLinkSourceCodeLens.ts` | CodeLens in source files showing reference counts |
| `codeLinkReferenceScanner.ts` | Scans documentation folders for code_link usage |
| `codeLinkDefinitionProvider.ts` | F12 "Go to Definition" for source attribute |
| `codeLinkDecorations.ts` | Editor decorations for code_link tags |

### CodeLens Registration
CodeLens providers are registered via `src/logic/codelens/codeLensRegister.ts` which is called from `pluginInit.ts`.

## Testing

Tests are in `src/test/` using Mocha. Run with `npm run test:xvfb` (Linux) or `npm test`.

- Tests use pure utility functions from `codeLinkTestUtils.ts` (no VS Code API dependency)
- Test files organized by feature: `validation.test.ts`, `highlight.test.ts`, `referenceScanner.test.ts`, etc.
- First-time Linux setup: `npm run test:setup` installs xvfb dependencies

## Development Commands

```bash
npm run watch      # Compile with webpack in watch mode
npm run lint       # ESLint
npm run test       # Run tests (requires compile-tests first)
npm run test:xvfb  # Run tests in headless mode (Linux)
npm run build      # Package VSIX
```

**Debug**: Press F5 to launch Extension Development Host. Extension activates when workspace contains `**/src/_configs/_config_primary.yml`.

## Key Files for Context

- Tag syntax patterns: `src/constants.ts` (`CODE_START_REGEX`, `SYMBOLS`)
- Workspace file loading: `src/logic/filesystem/workspaceFileLoader.ts`
- Grammar injection: `grammars/injections/kfmarkdown.json`

## Analysis

### A. Requirements Coverage
- The JIRA issue asked for: "Add missing editor-level validation across all tag definitions with reusable, generic validation rules"
- The PR adds 5 generic validation rules + dataType on all attributes + 2 new declarative properties (mutuallyExclusiveWith, dependsOn)
- Requirements appear fully covered. No obvious gaps or scope creep.

### B. Architecture Compliance
- **Definition-driven pattern**: ✅ New rules use declarative properties (mutuallyExclusiveWith, dependsOn) on TagAttribute definitions


- **TagNames enum**: N/A - no new tags
- **Definition registration**: N/A for tags; ✅ new rules registered in rulesRegister.ts

- **File naming**: ✅ Files follow `validate*.rule.ts` pattern
- **Grammar sync**: N/A - no grammar changes
- **Event system**: N/A - no new event listeners
- **Disposal**: N/A - no new disposables

I'm noticing an orphaned file that needs attention: `src/definitions/tags/block/card/diagnost` appears incomplete or misplaced in the structure.

Now looking at the TypeScript and code quality aspects. The implementation maintains strict typing with no `any` usage, properly extends the `TagAttribute` interface with optional fields, and consistently uses enums like `AttributeDataType`, `TagNames`, and `DiagnosticSeverity`. All imports are direct without barrel re-exports, there's no async code in the rules, linting passes, and JSDoc comments are present throughout. There's a potential issue with one of the validation rules that I should examine more closely. Looking at the import statement, `findTagAttributeNameRange` is definitely a value import that's never actually called in the code—only `createTagDiagnostic` gets used. The linter passes because TypeScript's unused locals check is disabled and ESLint doesn't have the rule configured, but it's still dead code that should be removed.

Now I'm reviewing the validation rules themselves. All five rules properly implement the expected function signature and are registered correctly. The diagnostic ranges look solid—most use the full tag range, though `validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue` smartly tries to pinpoint the exact attribute value range when possible before falling back to the broader tag range. For severity levels, duplicate attributes are marked as warnings which makes sense since they're problematic but potentially intentional, while empty required attributes are errors since they genuinely break functionality.

The test coverage is comprehensive with a new test file covering all five rules across positive cases, negative cases, and edge cases using Mocha and standard assertions.

Now I'm examining the regex pattern used in the duplicate attribute validation to see if it correctly identifies attribute names without false positives when values contain special characters like equals signs. in the value `"x=y"`? Let me think...

The regex runs on `afterTagName` which is `lang=csharp title="x=y" %}`. 
- First match: `lang` (followed by `=`) ✅
- Would `csharp` match? No, it's not followed by `=`.
- Would `title` match? Yes (followed by `=`) ✅
- Would `x` match? The text is `"x=y"`. The regex has `\b`, so `x` has a word boundary before it (after `"`), and `x` is followed by `=`. But wait, `\s*(?=\s*=)` means there can be whitespace between the word and `=`. In `"x=y"`, `x` is followed by `=` immediately. So `x` would match—this is a false positive.

Actually, let me reconsider the regex pattern more carefully: `/\b([\w-]+)\s*(?=\s*=)/gi`. The `\s*` before the lookahead consumes whitespace, and the lookahead checks for optional whitespace followed by `=`, which makes the `\s*` inside the lookahead somewhat redundant. Functionally, this matches any word followed by optional whitespace and then `=`. After the regex matches `title`, the position advances past that match, so the next potential match would start from somewhere after `title`.

So the duplicate detection regex would incorrectly flag content inside attribute values as attribute names, though a real false positive would only occur if the value contains a word-equals pattern that matches an actual attribute name elsewhere. The regex is flawed but the practical impact is limited.

I'm also noticing an unused import `findTagAttributeNameRange` in the validation rule file, and there's an orphaned file `imageAttrConflict.ts` that should be cleaned up.

Now looking at the grid values configuration, there's a type mismatch where `cols` declares `dataType: Number` but the `values` array contains strings like `'1'` and `'2'`. The type validation and allowed-value validation operate independently though—the `values` list restricts what's permitted while `dataType` checks the format, so this might not actually cause issues in practice.

However, there's an inconsistency across the codebase: `cell.types.ts` uses numeric values `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]` with `Number` dataType, while `grid.types.ts` uses string values `['1', '2', ...]` also with `Number` dataType. This inconsistency between how the two files represent their values should probably be addressed.

Actually, wait—looking at the PR changes more carefully, the grid values were already strings before this change. The PR only added the `Number` dataType to grid.types.ts, so this inconsistency is pre-existing, not something introduced here. And the validation logic handles this gracefully anyway by converting everything to strings before comparison, so it works correctly despite the mixed types.

Let me wrap up my analysis with the key findings I've identified. I'm realizing SUG-003 is actually a real correctness issue—the regex would produce false positives when attribute values contain patterns like `lang=y`, matching the attribute name twice. It's unlikely to occur in practice with KFM, but it's still a bug that should be flagged as a suggestion rather than blocking the review. I'm checking whether `document` is actually used in the `validateDuplicateAttributes` function—it's destructured from context but never referenced, though this matches the existing pattern in the codebase where other rules do the same thing, so it's not worth flagging.

# Phase 4: Aggregate & Deliver

## Before you begin

1. **Read `state.md`** at `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/state.md`
2. **Verify the current phase** — this skill is for Phase 4.
3. **Review completed phases** — confirm Phase 3 (Review Panel) is done.

## Instructions

### 1. Read all reviewer artifacts

For each reviewer that completed successfully, read:
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-opus/status.json`
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-opus/jira-findings.json`
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-gpt/status.json`
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-gpt/jira-findings.json`
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-gemini/status.json`
- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-gemini/jira-findings.json`

Skip any reviewer whose `status.json` shows `status: failed`.

### 2. Determine panel verdict

Apply the **unanimous approval rule**:
- ANY reviewer verdict of `needs-revision` → overall **NEEDS REVISION**
- Only unanimous `approved` → overall **APPROVED**
- If all successful reviewers approved but one failed, treat the panel verdict as the majority

### 3. Aggregate findings

Merge findings from all `jira-findings.json` files:
- Deduplicate by issue code + file + line — if multiple reviewers flag the same issue at the same location, keep the most detailed description and note which reviewers agreed
- Group by severity: Critical (must fix) → Style (should fix) → Suggestions (optional)
- Preserve the `code`, `file`, `line`, `detail`, and `correction` fields from each finding

### 4. Post unified JIRA comment

Post a single rich comment on **DOC-3141** with the panel verdict:

```
## Review Panel Verdict: APPROVED | NEEDS REVISION

**Panel:** 3 reviewers (Opus 4.6, GPT 5.4, Gemini Pro)
**Scout:** Build PASS | FAIL

### Reviewer Verdicts
| Reviewer | Verdict | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| malph-reviewer-opus | approved / needs-revision / failed | N findings |
| malph-reviewer-gpt | approved / needs-revision / failed | N findings |
| malph-reviewer-gemini | approved / needs-revision / failed | N findings |

### Aggregated Findings

#### Critical (must fix)
- **[ARCH-001]** `file:line` — description *(flagged by: opus, gpt)*

#### Style (should fix)
- **[TS-003]** `file:line` — description *(flagged by: gemini)*

#### Suggestions
- **[SUG-001]** description *(flagged by: opus)*

### Summary
<Brief overall assessment>
```

If APPROVED unanimously, keep it concise — the panel agrees the code is clean.

### 5. Update state.md

Record the panel verdict and finding counts.

## Before moving to the next phase

- `.ralph/tasks/DOC-3141/artifacts/malph-reviewer-gemini/jira-findings.json`

Skip any reviewer whose `status.json` shows `status: failed`.

### 2. Determine panel verdict

Apply the **unanimous approval rule**:
- ANY reviewer verdict of `needs-revision` → overall **NEEDS REVISION**
- Only unanimous `approved` → overall **APPROVED**
- If all successful reviewers approved but one failed, treat the panel verdict as the majority

arguments.content:
## What was reviewed

PR #2901 (`ralph/doc-3141` → `main`, version 1.2.7 → 1.2.8) adds **5 generic, reusable tag attribute validation rules** and extends the `TagAttribute` interface with two declarative properties. 39 files changed (767 ins, 46 del), 452 tests passing.

### The 5 new rules (all in `src/logic/diagnostics/tags/rules/`)
1. **validateDuplicateAttributes** — regex-based detection on raw tag text (dictionary would lose dupes)
2. **validateEmptyRequiredAttributeValue** — handles both positional (argv1) and named attrs
